labels.label: bbsrem:cuttachyon2

hypotheses.paper: x in a small disk U of dS^2, r a light-like ray from x in U
hypotheses.note: x = C.pt in dS^2; r = {[x + s w] : 0 < s < eps}, w a non-zero null vector of x^perp (GX.IsNullTangent), every eps > 0
gamma in Gamma_x minus {1}: gamma must fix x for the result to be a cone point at x; every such gamma is a boost, hence hyperbolic

hypotheses.paper: cut along r and glue back by gamma (figure fig.tachyon)
hypotheses.note: read on the link: l(x) cut at the direction of r, holonomy of the positive loop gamma^-1 if the positive sense crosses the cut from the glued copy into the other one, gamma otherwise (GX.cutGlueHol); the identification of the surgered disk with an open set of e(L) is argued, not formalized

hypotheses.paper: the future copy of r glued into the past copy (l.1303-1304)
hypotheses.note: future copy = the copy bounding the side of r in the future of the line of r (GX.FutureSide); the rule is the parameter src (true = printed)

hypotheses.paper: gamma is the inverse of the holonomy (l.1304)
hypotheses.note: replaced by the derived holonomy GX.cutGlueHol (library convention D(s+1) = f(D s): gamma^-1 when the positive sense crosses from the glued copy into the other, gamma otherwise); the paper's sentence is a convention statement tied to the figure and to the holonomy convention
both the l.915 form (IsPositive) and the l.908-913 repelling form (IsSpacelikePositiveRep)

hypotheses.paper: gamma y lies in the future/past of y
hypotheses.note: the causal order of dS^2 (CutGlue.IsCausalPast = GX.DSLe by definition)

hypotheses.paper: the resulting space is homeomorphic to the disk

findings: Convention-free: for any single side-of-line gluing rule, positivity of the surgery link does not depend on the orientation of r, only on the rule and on the direction gamma pushes r (isPositive_iff_past, isPositive_iff_future). Hence the two printed clauses (l.1307-1311: future-oriented r -> « future », past-oriented r -> « past ») cannot both hold under one rule; they hold together exactly when the copy glued by gamma is the one facing the space-like quadrant at x (bbsrem_cuttachyon2_reading).

Which clause fails depends on the holonomy sign convention. In the library's convention (IsLiftedDev: D(s+1) = f(D s), developing holonomy = gluing map^-1, positivity of l.908-915 read with it as in HSPositive), under the rule l.1303-1304 read literally, the future-oriented clause fails (GX.not_cuttachyon2_future_printed) and the past-oriented one holds. In the convention of the paper's worked examples (holonomy = gluing map: T_m l.1229-1233, bbsrem:positive_negative l.1239-1246, the AdS sentence l.1290-1296) every sign flips and the past-oriented clause fails. Not to be filed as a restatement before the convention is ruled.
l.1301 « a hyperbolic dS^2-isometry gamma » omits that gamma fixes x (needed for a cone point at x); every non-trivial element of Gamma_x is hyperbolic (GX.GammaP.exists_eq_dsBoost).
questions: The figure fig.tachyon (Chirtachyon.pstex_t) is not in the source. « Future copy of r » is read as the copy of r bounding the side of r lying in the future of the light-like line of r (for a future ray: the side of the time-like cone I+(x)). Is that the figure's convention?

Which holonomy sign convention is of record (extends OQ-120 (c)): l.908-915 read with the developing holonomy of IsLiftedDev (D(s+1) = f(D s), = gluing map^-1, the library's), or with the gluing-map holonomy of the paper's worked examples (T_m l.1229-1233, l.1239-1246, l.1290-1296)? The answer decides which printed clause of cuttachyon2 fails, and may bear on earlier signs (HSPositive, GX.exists_positive_negative). The master opens the OQ row.

Which correction is of record, once the convention is ruled: change the failing clause (in the library's convention, « future » -> « past » at l.1308; in the paper's, « past » -> « future » at l.1310), or keep both clauses and change the rule to « the copy facing the space-like quadrant is glued into the copy facing the time-like cone »? All three are proved (isPositive_iff_past, isPositive_iff_future, bbsrem_cuttachyon2_reading).

The surgery is formalized on its link (the circle l(x) cut at the direction of r and glued, with the holonomy rule of l.1304); that the surgered disk is HS-isomorphic near x to an open set of e(L) is argued (the suspension of the cut direction is the light-like geodesic through r), not formalized. Accept the link-level reading?

labels.label: bbsrem:however_no_positive_negative

hypotheses.note: the types btzPast, btzFuture, extremeBTZ b of GX.LinkType (HasType); the general lemmas hold for every degree-0 circle (Misner and cuspidal too)

questions: « No positive/negative dichotomy » (l.1481) is read as: every BTZ-like circle, extreme or not, is positive in the sense of GX.GammaLinkCircle.IsPositive (its clauses concern time-like points and degrees >= 2, so they are vacuous at degree 0); none is positive or negative in any of the four signed senses of l.906-922 (IsSpacelikePositive/Negative, IsLightlikePositive/Negative, which need a degree k >= 1); and for every oriented lifted pair the holonomy has a fixed point and the inequality of l.915 read at degree 0 (D s < f (D s)) holds, its reverse holding on I+ only when I+ is empty (BTZ-like future). So no sign splits a type. Is that the intended content, or is an isomorphism statement meant (e.g. the circles of holonomy g and g^-1 on the same interval coincide)? The reading rests on the types of OQ-116 (b) and OQ-135, and occurrence of these types is not formalized (OQ-135 (c)). The likely intended content (by contrast with l.926-932) is that BTZ-like circles of holonomy g and g^-1 at the same p are isomorphic; that is not proved, so the row stays partial.

kb_proposals: The positive sense of linkCover is vol3 x's (GX.CutGlue.vol3_linkCover_pos: t < t' < t+1 gives vol3 x (lift t) (lift t') > 0); a lift g with a fixed point of A in Gamma_x moves t up iff the lifts of (linkCover t, A . linkCover t) are a direct pair (GX.CutGlue.sign_of_lift).

At x in dS^2 the lift with a fixed point of GammaP.dsBoost hx zeta moves the future time-like directions up iff 0 < zeta * vol3 x (dsE₀ x) (jVec x) (GX.CutGlue.future_up_iff); every vector of x^perp is a e₀ + b j (GX.CutGlue.exists_frame_comb).

Cut-and-glue along a light-like ray of dS^2 is GX.GammaLinkCircle.IsCutGlueLink w gamma src; in the library's holonomy convention (D(s+1) = f(D s)) and src = true it is positive iff gamma pushes the ray into its own past, for both orientations of the ray (…isPositive_iff_past). The paper's worked examples use the inverse convention.
GX.CutGlue.IsCausalPast tau sigma is GX.DSLe tau sigma of HSCausal by definition (hyp = dsHat), restated to avoid importing a module in flight; unify at graduation.
